items.q: The sum of the ages of Billy and his sister is 32. If Billy is 8 years older than his sister, what are their ages?
items.src: Cambridge Essential Mathematics 9 (3rd Ed), Ch 2 review, short answer Q15 (p. 165)

items.q: The perimeter around the top of a rectangular billiard table is 810 cm. The length is twice the width. Use $l$ and $w$ to write two linear equations, then solve them to find the dimensions of the top of the billiard table.
items.src: Oxford Maths 10 VC (2022), Exercise 4F Q14a–c (p. 204); adapted: three parts combined

items.q: Sophie has decided to make hand-painted cards. She invests \$60 in a set of paintbrushes and enough paint to make 40 cards. The cost of each plain white card is \$2 and she plans to sell the painted cards for \$6 each. The cost is $a = 2n + 60$ and the money received is $a = 6n$. What are the coordinates of the point of intersection of the two graphs? What does this tell you?
sol: Selling 15 cards recovers the \$90 spent (break even).
items.src: Oxford Maths 10 VC (2022), Exercise 4F Q13d (p. 204); adapted: parts a, b given in the stem

items.q: Mila plants $820$ hectares of potatoes and corn. To maximise his profit he plants $140$ hectares more of potatoes than of corn. How many hectares of each does he plant?
items.src: Cambridge Essential Mathematics 9 (3rd Ed), Exercise 2K Q2 (p. 153)

items.q: Mal bought three bottles of milk and four bags of chips for a total of \$17. At the same shop, Barbara bought one bottle of milk and five bags of chips for \$13. Find how much each bottle of milk and each bag of chips cost.
items.src: Cambridge Essential Mathematics 9 (3rd Ed), Exercise 2K Q3 (p. 154); adapted: steps a–d left out
